home.title: Four courts. One board.
home.description: Take a seat around the 8×8 board. Roll two dice, move the matching piece types, and score captured pieces as four armies compete.
home.note: A source-based reconstruction of the historical dice game; uncertain procedures are marked as choices.
home.aboutBody: This playable ruleset follows Al-Biruni’s account as compared with later historical research. Some details are not settled by the sources, so this edition names its digital choices in the rules notes.

bot.title: Take one seat
bot.body: Choose an army and a computer level. The other three seats play independently.
bot.thinking: The computer is choosing a move.

game.title: Chaturaji
game.moveHint: Choose a {{piece}} for the highlighted die, then tap a marked square.
game.noMoves: Moves and dice rolls will appear here.
game.resultBody: The third original King was captured. Final points decide the winner.

tutorial.title: Learn at the board
tutorial.exercisePrompt: Select a Red piece and make a legal move on the board.
tutorial.makeMove: The current result is {{face}}. Make one legal Red move on the board.
tutorial.completeBody: You have covered the selected movement, dice, scoring, promotion and ending rules. Start a game and learn the rhythm of all four seats.

diagram.seats: Each army begins in a corner, facing toward the middle.
diagram.turn-order: Play moves clockwise around the board.
diagram.dice: Use each result for one eligible piece action.
diagram.movement: A piece may move only when its type matches the current die.
diagram.pawns: Pawns advance outward toward the opposite edge.
diagram.check: Kings are captured like other pieces; there is no check rule.
diagram.scoring: Captured pieces add their printed value to your score.
diagram.promotion: A pawn reaching its far edge promotes to a piece already captured.
diagram.boat-triumph: A Boat reaching the opposite Boat corner captures the enemy King.
diagram.throne: A King landing on its allied throne can take control of that army.
diagram.ending: After three original Kings fall, the highest score wins.

four-armies.title: Four armies share the board
four-armies.body: Red, Green, Yellow and Black each begin in a corner with a King, Elephant, Horse, Boat and four Pawns. Which statement is true?

turn-order.title: Move clockwise
turn-order.body: Red takes the first turn. Seats then act clockwise. Which army follows Red?

dice-one-five.title: Read a one or a five
dice-one-five.body: The dice select which pieces may act. A one and a five have the same choices. Which pieces are eligible?

make-a-move.title: Try a move
make-a-move.body: Only a piece type allowed by the current die can move. The board marks the legal destinations for the selected piece.

dice-two-three.title: A two or a three
dice-two-three.body: Each die result names a piece type for one action. What does a two allow?

elephant-and-boat.title: Long moves and a diagonal jump
elephant-and-boat.body: The Elephant slides like a rook. The Boat makes a single two-square diagonal jump, even if the middle square is occupied. What does a six allow?

pawns.title: Pawns advance outward
pawns.body: Each Pawn advances toward the opposite edge from its starting side. Pawns move one square forward and capture one square diagonally forward. Can a Pawn move two squares on its first move?

no-check.title: There is no check
no-check.body: The King moves one square in any direction. In this reconstruction, Kings are captured like other pieces; players do not announce or escape check. What happens when a King is attacked?
options: Nothing special; it can be captured.

capture-points.title: Captures add points
capture-points.body: A captured Pawn is worth 1, Boat 2, Horse 3, Elephant 4 and King 5. How many points is a captured Horse worth?

promotion.title: Promotion uses your capture pool
promotion.body: When a Pawn reaches the far edge, it promotes to a piece type you have already captured. What must you have to promote to a Horse?
options: A captured Horse in your pool
A Horse still on the board

boat-triumph.title: The Boat has a triumph
boat-triumph.body: A Boat that reaches the opposite Boat’s corner captures that army’s King. This is the Boat triumph. What does it capture there?

allied-throne.title: An allied throne can change control
allied-throne.body: Each army has an opposite ally. If your King lands on your ally’s throne, you take control of that army too. Which armies are allied in this edition?

game-end.title: Three captured Kings end the game
game-end.body: The game ends when three original Kings have been captured. Scores are then compared; the top score wins, and a tied top score shares the win. How many original Kings must fall?

online.title: Invite three players
online.body: Create a private room and share its link. Each seat reconnects to its original army. The server checks every move and dice result.
online.inviteBody: Share this private room link. All four seats must join before the first move.
online.full: This room already has four seats.
online.invalid: Enter a valid six-character room code.
online.unavailable: The room service is unavailable. Try again.
online.copyFailed: Could not copy the invite link. Copy the address from your browser.

errors.room-full: This room already has four seats.
